name: Jehdeiah
overview: Jehdeiah was a male figure identified as the Meronothite who held responsibility over King David's donkeys, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:30. There is no information about his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this role. His position indicates a trusted administrative function within David's household.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehdeiah means 'YHWH rejoices [in his works],' reflecting a theophoric element that honors God. This proper name, mentioned in 1 Chronicles 27:30, does not appear to have been given directly by God but conveys a meaningful connection to the Lord's joy in human endeavors.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Jehdeiah beyond his designation as the Meronothite in charge of David's donkeys. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jehdeiah's significance lies in his administrative role during King David's reign, overseeing a specific aspect of the royal household's operations. His mention highlights the organized structure of David's kingdom and the importance of faithful management of resources. Although a minor figure, Jehdeiah's service contributes to the broader narrative of God's providence through David's governance.
